general.label: Technical Implementation & Integration
general.description: Components are genuinely connected and working (not a mock-up); design choices are sound and explainable.

general.label: Testing, Validation & Reliability
general.description: Measured results, edge cases handled, failures analysed and reported honestly.

general.label: Development Progress & Ownership
general.description: Verified progress since Round 1, feedback addressed, and each member can explain their own part.

general.label: Deployment & Real-World Readiness
general.description: Usable by target users, with data privacy, documentation and maintainability covered.

general.label: Technical Demonstration & Q&A
general.description: Live demo, clear answers, honest about limitations.

general_text.label: Judge Notes (Internal)
general_text.description: Private notes and observations for the jury panel.

general_text.label: Team Feedback
general_text.description: Constructive feedback visible to the participants.

PSE01.title: AI-Assisted Tele-Triage Companion for ASHA/PHC Workers
PSE01.decisiveTest: Disconnect the internet and give a local-language symptom/vitals input. Verify the triage output and referral note, then restore the network and check the PHC sync.

criteria.label: On-device triage correctness
criteria.description: Red / yellow / green flags are produced from symptoms and vitals with no cloud call. Outputs on relevant test cases are consistent with clinical guidelines.

criteria.label: Local-language voice intake
criteria.description: The ASHA worker can enter symptoms and vitals in a regional language. Transcription reliably preserves clinically important details.

criteria.label: Referral note and actionable output
criteria.description: A clear referral note for the PHC doctor, with relevant symptoms, vitals and the triage reason.

criteria.label: Offline operation and deferred sync
criteria.description: Intake and triage work without internet. Records sync reliably once connectivity returns, with no duplicates or data loss.

criteria.label: Clinical safety and uncertainty handling
criteria.description: Red flags escalate appropriately. Uncertain or incomplete input never gives unsafe reassurance. The system makes no false diagnosis claim.

PSE02.title: Smartphone-Based Non-Invasive Anaemia Screening
PSE02.decisiveTest: Use good-quality and deliberately poor-quality images. Inspect the Hb estimate, confidence handling and the retake/escalation response.
PSE02.notes: Classification accuracy alone, or one successful screenshot, does not prove Hb estimation reliability.

criteria.label: Hb estimation and output validity
criteria.description: A numerical Hb estimate (or clearly defined Hb output) is generated from the image; appropriate error metrics are reported on held-out labelled data.

criteria.label: Robustness across capture conditions
criteria.description: Performance is tested across different lighting, phone cameras and skin tones; limitations are measured, not just claimed.

criteria.label: Low-confidence escalation
criteria.description: Poor-quality images and uncertain predictions are detected; a repeat capture or confirmatory blood-test referral is given.

criteria.label: Image capture and quality control
criteria.description: Consistent capture instructions, usable-image checks, and a rejection or retake workflow for blurred or poorly lit images.

criteria.label: Clinical validation and honest reporting
criteria.description: Test set, sample limitations, error distribution and intended-use boundaries are documented; not presented as a substitute for lab-confirmed diagnosis.

PSE03.title: Immunisation Dropout Prediction and Recall
PSE03.decisiveTest: Add one high-risk child and one on-time vaccination history to synthetic records. Compare risk ranking, next-dose date and reminder workflow.

criteria.label: Dropout risk prediction
criteria.description: Next-dose dropout risk is estimated from dose history, punctuality, geography or other relevant features, with proper validation and baseline comparison.

criteria.label: Risk-ranked ASHA visit list
criteria.description: High-risk children appear in priority order; the ranking helps field workers make actionable decisions.

criteria.label: Proactive reminder workflow
criteria.description: Timely SMS/IVR reminders are generated from the next-dose schedule and risk, supporting the parent’s language.

criteria.label: Scheduling and follow-up logic
criteria.description: Due dates, upcoming doses, missed-dose states and follow-up status are handled correctly.

criteria.label: Prediction quality and privacy
criteria.description: Model evaluation, false negatives/positives and data limitations are documented; child and parent records are protected.

PSE04.title: Voice-First Multilingual Agri-Advisory
PSE04.decisiveTest: Ask one supported crop-advisory query, one location/season-specific query and one out-of-scope question. Verify sources and unsupported-answer handling.

criteria.label: Grounded agricultural answers
criteria.description: Responses to crop, sowing window, irrigation and input-use queries are supported by ICAR/KVK or another approved advisory source.

criteria.label: Voice-first regional-language interaction
criteria.description: The farmer can speak and receive an understandable response; interaction in a supported language is practical.

criteria.label: Source traceability and hallucination control
criteria.description: Each answer identifies its source or advisory context; unsupported questions show uncertainty instead of invented advice.

criteria.label: Farmer-specific relevance
criteria.description: Advice fits the crop, location/season and question context; unsupported context is clearly identified.

criteria.label: Accessible phone/WhatsApp workflow
criteria.description: The full query-to-answer flow works on the chosen channel; the demo is not limited to a static chatbot screen.

PSE05.title: Adaptive Peer Learning Network
PSE05.decisiveTest: Input students with different performance profiles. Check whether groups, quizzes and pace recommendations change logically with their learning gaps.
PSE05.notes: Facial emotion is not definitive proof of understanding; the system should treat it as an imperfect signal.

criteria.label: Adaptive peer grouping
criteria.description: Meaningful clusters form from student performance data; each group’s strengths and weaknesses can be explained.

criteria.label: Group-specific micro-quizzes
criteria.description: Quiz questions are generated or selected for each group’s identified gaps; content is relevant and answerable.

criteria.label: Engagement/confusion estimation
criteria.description: A webcam workflow identifies broad categories (engaged, confused, disengaged); limitations and prediction errors are acknowledged.

criteria.label: Teaching pace adjustment
criteria.description: The signal leads to an actionable pace suggestion or adaptation, not just an emotion label.

criteria.label: Learning-loop evidence
criteria.description: Quiz results or later performance refine the grouping or learning recommendation.

PSE06.title: Smart Sign Language Learning & Real-Time Translation App
PSE06.decisiveTest: Show known gestures, unseen examples and no-sign/background frames to the live camera. Inspect recognition, latency and learning mode.
PSE06.notes: If the team recognises only letters, do not score it as full sign-language sentence translation. Claimed scope must match actual functionality.

criteria.label: Sign/gesture recognition correctness
criteria.description: Supported signs or letters are recognised correctly; results are reported on representative held-out examples.

criteria.label: Real-time performance
criteria.description: Recognition and translated output appear with practical latency from camera frames; failure conditions are tested.

criteria.label: Learning-mode effectiveness
criteria.description: Students can learn and practise signs with examples, feedback or recognition-based practice, not just a translation screen.

criteria.label: Robustness and uncertainty handling
criteria.description: Tested with different users, camera positions or backgrounds; unknown or ambiguous gestures are not confidently mislabelled.

criteria.label: Accessible communication output
criteria.description: Recognised signs/letters become usable text or other supported output, with a clear user workflow.

PSE07.title: AI-Based Investor Fraud & Impersonation Detection
PSE07.decisiveTest: Test one benign media sample, one known manipulated sample, and suspicious versus normal adviser text. Verify the result, evidence and alert.
PSE07.notes: No marks for a detection layer the team did not implement. Public benchmark data is acceptable.

criteria.label: Deepfake media detection
criteria.description: Supported video/audio inputs are analysed for manipulation risk; performance and false alarms are reported on benchmark/test examples.

criteria.label: Impersonation detection
criteria.description: Chat/profile text is checked for fake financial-adviser claims, suspicious urgency or other impersonation indicators; triggered signals can be explained.

criteria.label: Fake trading-app indicators
criteria.description: A practical mechanism flags suspicious apps from listing/interface metadata or defined indicators, with evidence and limitations.

criteria.label: Risk aggregation and actionable alerts
criteria.description: Signals combine into an understandable risk result or alert, with supporting reasons for the user.

criteria.label: Robustness and uncertainty
criteria.description: Benign and manipulated/suspicious examples are tested; an uncertain result is not presented as confirmed fraud.

PSE08.title: Tokenized, Privacy-Preserving KYC Framework
PSE08.decisiveTest: Have an institution request only an age/address-type attribute. Verify that after consent only the required attribute is shared, not the full KYC record. Also test an invalid/tampered token.
PSE08.notes: Issuing a token alone does not prove privacy-preserving KYC. Inspect the actual disclosure boundary and verification process.

criteria.label: Credential/token issuance and verification
criteria.description: The KYC provider issues a verified credential/token; the requesting institution can verify its validity.

criteria.label: Consent and selective disclosure
criteria.description: The customer gives consent and only the requested KYC attributes are shared; the institution is not exposed to the full underlying record.

criteria.label: Privacy and security controls
criteria.description: Safeguards against unauthorised access, token tampering, replay and inappropriate data exposure are demonstrated.

criteria.label: End-to-end verification workflow
criteria.description: Provider → issuance → consent → institution request → selective disclosure → verification runs as one integrated flow.

criteria.label: Auditability and user control
criteria.description: Verification requests, consent and disclosure events have a traceable audit; the customer gets an understandable record of sharing.

PSE10.title: AI-Based Personalised Internship & Skill Recommendation Engine
PSE10.decisiveTest: Input two contrasting student profiles and one internship listing. Verify the recommendations and skill-gap analysis change meaningfully when the student’s skills change.

criteria.label: Personalised internship matching
criteria.description: Relevant internships are ranked using academic record, projects, certifications and skills; reasons for matches can be explained.

criteria.label: Skill-gap analysis
criteria.description: Student skills are compared with internship requirements to identify missing skills; gaps trace back to actual role requirements.

criteria.label: Targeted course recommendations
criteria.description: Relevant courses from SWAYAM or another suitable catalogue address the identified gaps.

criteria.label: Recommendation relevance and transparency
criteria.description: Irrelevant listings are reduced; skill match, missing requirements and ranking logic are understandable.

criteria.label: Student accessibility and profile workflow
criteria.description: Students can input/update their profile; intended language support and a usable end-to-end recommendation workflow exist.

PSE11.title: The Real-Time DPDPA Compliance Monitoring Agent
PSE11.decisiveTest: Run four controlled cases: permitted attribute, purpose-mismatched attribute, raw PII in logs, incomplete erasure request. After each, verify the correct violation, displayed reason and suitable remediation.
PSE11.notes: Six teams are on this PS: use the same test-event pack, criterion weights and scoring anchors for all six. Do not give marks for dashboard polish when compliance detection is missing.

criteria.label: Data minimisation and purpose limitation
criteria.description: API/database attributes are evaluated against the declared processing purpose; unnecessary or unauthorised collection is flagged.

criteria.label: Unmasked PII leakage detection
criteria.description: Raw phone, PAN, email or other defined sensitive fields in simulated logs are detected, with the event and reason identified.

criteria.label: Retention and erasure auditing
criteria.description: Missing expiry labels are detected; after a simulated erasure request, incomplete deletion across storage-layer stubs is flagged.

criteria.label: Real-time pipeline, dashboard and remediation
criteria.description: Ingestion → compliance rules → alert/dashboard works end-to-end, showing violation count, status, rule/clause and actionable remediation.

PSE12.title: Real-Time Transaction Fraud Detection
PSE12.decisiveTest: Run a normal transaction, a high-value transaction, an unusual-hour/location case and a multiple-signal case. Compare risk scores with triggering reasons.

criteria.label: Fraud signal coverage
criteria.description: Transaction-value threshold, unusual day/hour, location mismatch and unusual purchase pattern are all evaluated appropriately.

criteria.label: Risk scoring and detection quality
criteria.description: Rules/ML produce a risk score or level; suitable metrics and a baseline comparison on labelled test data are available.

criteria.label: Explainability of flagged transactions
criteria.description: The judge gets a clear reason: which rule or signal triggered and why the transaction looks suspicious.

criteria.label: Real-time alert workflow
criteria.description: A risk result and alert are produced in practical runtime after a transaction is input; the event traces back to the transaction.

criteria.label: False-positive handling and validation
criteria.description: Legitimate unusual transactions and known fraud examples are tested; false alarms and missed-fraud limits are documented.

PSE13.title: Health Screening Assistant
PSE13.decisiveTest: Input low-risk, high-risk and several same-locality synthetic patient records. Inspect the risk result, facility ranking and aggregate alert.
PSE13.notes: Disease-prediction accuracy is not medical validity. The team must explain test data, limitations and intended screening use.

criteria.label: Symptom-based risk assessment
criteria.description: Symptom intake produces a risk tier and possible disease category; test cases and classifier limitations are documented.

criteria.label: Healthcare facility recommendation
criteria.description: Facilities are ranked by location, distance and required service; the nearest facility alone is not enough if its service is unsuitable.

criteria.label: Aggregated facility alerts
criteria.description: Multiple screening records produce catchment-area caseload or risk-cluster summaries; the relevant facility gets an actionable notification.

criteria.label: Safe screening and escalation
criteria.description: High-risk symptoms trigger escalation; uncertainty and limitations are clear; output does not claim a definitive diagnosis.

criteria.label: End-to-end screening workflow
criteria.description: Symptom entry to risk output, facility recommendation and alerting works as one integrated workflow.

PSE14.title: ClaimPilot AI
PSE14.decisiveTest: Using the team’s selected modules, run real/synthetic claim documents, duplicate claim records or vehicle damage images. Verify the outputs perform actual verification, fraud detection or cost estimation.
PSE14.notes: The team declares its two modules before judging; no penalty for the third. A UI mock-up alone is not a completed module.

criteria.label: First selected module: depth and validation
criteria.description: The module is genuinely implemented and validated on relevant test cases (document extraction and rule checks, fraud-signal detection, or damage severity and repair-cost range).

criteria.label: Second selected module: depth and validation
criteria.description: The module is genuinely implemented and validated on relevant test cases (document extraction and rule checks, fraud-signal detection, or damage severity and repair-cost range).

criteria.label: Integration into claim workflow
criteria.description: Selected modules work in one coherent claim workflow; output is reviewable, reasons/uncertainties are shown, and there is no unsupported automatic approval or rejection.

PSE15.title: AI-Powered Crew Assembly for Event Staffing (CrewForge AI)
PSE15.decisiveTest: Configure an event with a tight budget, some unavailable candidates, and a required role whose preferred candidate is unsuitable. Check that the system assembles a feasible complete crew within budget with useful backups.
PSE15.notes: Do not score CrewForge as a search/filter app. The central challenge is joint constrained optimisation.

criteria.label: Joint crew optimisation
criteria.description: A complete crew is assembled, not a list of individually top-rated candidates; required roles are covered with skill-fit, availability, proximity, reliability and budget considered jointly.

criteria.label: Budget and constraint satisfaction
criteria.description: Total crew cost is within budget; role coverage and availability constraints hold; if no feasible crew exists, the violation is clearly reported.

criteria.label: Ranked backup candidates and no-show resilience
criteria.description: A ranked backup list exists for every required role; backups fit on skills, availability, location and reliability.

criteria.label: Candidate matching and reliability logic
criteria.description: Skills, ratings, location, calendar overlap and past collaboration success are appropriately used in selection.

criteria.label: Event-specific adaptability
criteria.description: Changing event type, date, location, budget or required roles meaningfully updates the crew.

PSE09.title: AI-Driven Crop Price Forecasting & Market Routing App
PSE09.decisiveTest: Run forecasting model on price history; inspect price trend projection and routing recommendations.
PSE09.notes: Check accuracy across seasonal variations and market volatility.

criteria.label: Price Forecasting Accuracy & Validation
criteria.description: Price prediction model validity on historical data and error analysis across seasonal variations.

criteria.label: Market Routing & Logistics Optimization
criteria.description: Practicality and optimality of market selection, transport cost estimation, and net profit advice for farmers.
